page: Amazon Web Services r8a.24xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 96 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware vector support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instruction sets.

Memory capacity is configured at 768 GB of DDR5 operating at 6000 MT/s, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The memory subsystem delivers 515.99 GB/s in large-block uncached read bandwidth and 215.11 GB/s in write bandwidth. The instance includes a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems. Hardware graphics accelerators are absent.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute and data-processing tasks, scoring 31,789 on Geekbench multi-core and 139,965 on PassMark CPU. High-throughput in-memory handling is evident in Redis benchmark execution, achieving 253.4 million SET operations per second, alongside 41,791.81 in PassMark database operations. In LLM inference tests, CPU-based prompt processing achieves 378.95 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The 1:1 physical core allocation minimizes noisy neighbor interference and virtualization latency overhead. Operating without integrated local storage means all IOPS rely on external network-attached volumes, introducing potential bandwidth competition with standard network traffic. The instance offers strong resource efficiency for infrastructure demanding dense DDR5 memory allocations without GPU overhead. Best-fit applications include distributed in-memory databases, large Redis clusters, enterprise real-time analytics, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.24xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 96 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping. The system allocates 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 GB-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is anchored by a 40 Gbps baseline interface. The instance features no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier processing power, registering a multi-core Geekbench score of 31,789 and 253.4 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 515.99 GB/s on uncached reads. This compute and memory profile is well suited for memory-bound relational databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise analytics, and intensive batch ETL processing.
